title: Blood test for allergies
what: A blood test that looks for antibodies to different allergens: pollen, dust, pet hair, and foods. Skin tests are not needed for it.
why: For a runny nose, sneezing, rash, itching, or cough that comes from certain things or in a certain season.
duration: usually 5 minutes; blood is taken from a vein
tell_doctor: What you think you react to, and what the reaction looks like
If you are getting allergy treatment by shots or under the tongue

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Usually you do not need to fast. Some labs ask you to come in the morning, 3 to 4 hours after eating. Check with your clinic.

prepare.title: Allergy medicines
prepare.text: They usually do not affect the blood test, unlike skin tests. Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor, who will decide.

bring: Your referral with the list of allergens, if the doctor gave you one
steps: You sit down and rest your arm on the armrest
A band is tightened above your elbow
The skin is wiped, and blood is taken from a vein
A cotton ball is pressed on the spot
feel: Sometimes a small bruise stays afterwards
after: You can eat and go about your day right away
Results usually come in a few days, depending on how many allergens are tested
An allergist explains the result. Antibodies do not always mean a real allergy

faq.q: Can I have the allergy test while taking allergy pills?
faq.a: Usually yes. They hardly affect the blood test. It is skin tests that need a break from them.

faq.q: If the test found antibodies, do I definitely have an allergy?
faq.a: Not always. The doctor compares the result with how you feel. Sometimes there are antibodies but no reaction.

faq.q: Can a child have an allergy blood test?
faq.a: Yes, the blood test is fine for children too. The doctor will say which allergens to check.
